process.desc: We evaluate your existing garage floor for cracks, spalling, settling, oil stains, and moisture issues. We measure door threshold heights to confirm there's room for new concrete thickness.

process.title: Removal or Prep
process.desc: For full replacement, we break out and haul away the old floor. For resurfacing, we grind or shot-blast the existing surface to create a proper bonding profile and remove contaminants.

process.title: Repair & Base Work
process.desc: Cracks and damaged areas are repaired. For new floors, we install gravel base and vapor barrier. The floor area is formed and leveled to ensure proper drainage toward the garage door.

process.title: Pour or Apply
process.desc: New floors are poured at 4 to 5 inch thickness with wire mesh reinforcement. For overlays, the resurfacing material is applied to the specified thickness. We finish with a smooth trowel for the best surface under coatings.

process.title: Coating & Protection
process.desc: After curing, we apply your chosen protective finish — penetrating sealer, epoxy coating, or polyurea coating. Each provides different levels of chemical resistance, appearance, and durability.

faqs.q: What's the best coating for a garage floor?
faqs.a: Epoxy coatings are the most popular choice — they create a glossy, chemical-resistant surface that handles vehicle traffic well. Cost is $5 to $8 per square foot applied. Polyurea coatings are more flexible and cure faster but cost more ($8 to $12 per square foot). Penetrating sealers are the most affordable option ($2 to $4 per square foot) and protect without changing the appearance. Each option has trade-offs between durability, appearance, and cost.

faqs.q: How much does a new garage floor cost?
faqs.a: A full garage floor replacement (2-car garage, 400-500 sq ft) typically costs $3,200 to $5,000, which includes removal of the old floor, base preparation, new 4-inch slab, and basic sealer. Adding an epoxy or polyurea coating adds $2,000 to $4,000. Resurfacing an existing floor with an overlay costs $2,000 to $4,000 if the existing slab is structurally sound.

faqs.q: Can you fix a garage floor that's sinking or uneven?
faqs.a: Yes, depending on the severity. Minor settling (under 1 inch) can be addressed with mudjacking or polyurethane foam injection to lift the slab back to level. Severe settling or structural cracking usually requires full removal and replacement with proper base preparation. We'll assess the cause of the settling and recommend the most cost-effective solution.

faqs.q: How long does a garage floor project take?
faqs.a: Full replacement takes 2 to 3 days — demolition and base prep (1 day), pour and finish (1 day). The floor needs 7 days before parking vehicles on it. If adding an epoxy or polyurea coating, that takes an additional 1-2 days after the concrete has cured for 28 days. Resurfacing existing floors takes 1-2 days.

garage-floors.considerations: Measure your garage door threshold before adding concrete thickness — you need clearance for the door to seal properly. If your garage has a floor drain, ensure it's functional and properly connected before covering it with new concrete. Consider your garage's primary use (parking vs workshop) when choosing the finish.
garage-floors.materials: 4,000 PSI concrete, 6x6 welded wire mesh, vapor barrier, 4 inches compacted gravel base, expansion joint material at walls, smooth trowel finish, and your chosen protective coating — penetrating sealer, epoxy system (primer, base coat, clear coat), or polyurea coating.
garage-floors.timeline: Full replacement: 2-3 days for demo, base prep, and pour. Allow 7 days before parking. Epoxy/polyurea coating: 1-2 days application, 24-72 hours cure before foot traffic, 5-7 days before parking. Resurfacing: 1-2 days with 3-5 days cure time before vehicles.
garage-floors.priceFactors: Garage size (square footage), removal of existing floor, base preparation, slab thickness, coating type (sealer, epoxy, polyurea), crack repair needs, moisture mitigation, floor drain work, and threshold adjustments.
